title: A category with no account posts to ShopView Review
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location is connected to QuickBooks Online, with Inventory Asset and Cost of Parts mapped on its ShopView Accounts page, and that AccountingHub is not enabled.
  • Have access to the QuickBooks Online company of the test location, so its journal entries can be read.
  • Make sure Require Review Before Completion is off in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a new No Charge category for this test, category A, with no QuickBooks account.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A.
  • Have a new No Charge work order for this test, work order 1, for customer A, category category A, in status Complete, with one approved line with one stock part picked from inventory at a cost of $40.00 each, quantity 2.
  • Make sure Goodwill is mapped to an account, so another category's row is filled.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Click Close Work Order in the work order header.
  3. Click Close Work Order in the confirmation.
  4. In QuickBooks Online, open the journal entries for work order 1's number.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The Close confirmation opens.

Step 3:

  • The work order shows the status Closed.

Step 4:

  • The entry debits the ShopView Review account $80.00, not Goodwill's account.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11762 (Story 5, QuickBooks Online account mapping), story SV-11764 (Story 7, QuickBooks Online sync)

  • S7-N2: “If no expense account is mapped (with Inventory Asset and Cost of Parts mapped; otherwise S7-N5), the entries post to the ShopView Review expense account, as every unmapped account does today (the sync creates it in the shop's QuickBooks if needed), and the accountant reclasses them in QuickBooks. If the mapped account was deleted or made inactive in QuickBooks, the entry fails as it does for every other row today and shows in QB Unexported until the row is fixed or the entry is exported by hand (S5-E1). Close is not blocked and nothing is shown to the advisor beyond S3-N4, which covers the unmapped case.”
  • S5-E2: “If a category row is empty, the parts cost of that category's work orders and lines posts to the ShopView Review account (S5-R4); there is no fallback from one category row to another.”
  • S5-R4: “While a category row is empty, the row shows the existing empty-row hint with the text "Not set. Parts cost of [category] work orders posts to the ShopView Review account until you pick one." There is no fallback from one row to another. While the setting is off, empty rows show no hint.”
  • Terminology: “ShopView Review → the expense account the QuickBooks sync creates in the shop's QuickBooks and posts to whenever a mapped account is missing, deleted or inactive. Existing behaviour.”
